test.title: Magnetic Effects of Current - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: The fractional change in the magnetic field intensity at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> from centre on the axis of current carrying coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> to the magnetic field intensity at the centre of the same coil is: (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>)

A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ is in an electric and magnetic field given by

$$

\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j} ; \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=4 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}

$$

The charged particle is shifted from the origin to the point $\mathrm{P}(x=1 ; y=1)$ along a straight path. The magnitude of the total work done is :

Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn></msub></math>. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> will be:

If their moments of inertia are in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math> then the ratio of their magnetic moments will be

A coil is placed in magnetic field such that plane of coil is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. The magnetic flux through a coil can be changed:

A. By changing the magnitude of the magnetic field within the coil.

B. By changing the area of coil within the magnetic field.

C. By changing the angle between the direction of magnetic field and the plane of the coil.

D. By reversing the magnetic field direction abruptly without changing its magnitude.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

A rectangular loop of sides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>  and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> with current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is in Y-Z plane. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface?

(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and $B_2 \gt B_1$)

question.text: A bar magnet with a magnetic moment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is placed in parallel position relative to a magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The amount of required work done in turning the magnet form parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is ________.

A straight wire carrying a current of 14 A is bent into a semicircular arc of radius 2.2 cm as shown in the figure. The magnetic field produced by the current at the centre O of the arc is ____ × 10–4 T

A charge of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is moving with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> along the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-axis under a magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of strength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The force acting on the charge is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

Two long parallel wires $X$ and $Y$, separated by a distance of 6 cm , carry currents of 5A and 4A, respectively, in opposite directions as shown in the figure. Magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at point P at a distance of 4 cm from wire Y is $x \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $x$ is__________ . Take permeability of free space as $\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{SI}$ units.

A long solenoid with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>turns</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> has a core material with relative permeability <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn></math> and volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></math> If the core material is replaced by another material having relative permeability of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn></math> with same volume maintaining same current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the solenoid, the fractional change in the magnetic moment of the core would be approximately <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>499</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from its center is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The magnetic moment of the dipole is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. (Given : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
